claims.claim: Jensen Huang was born 17 February 1963 in Tainan, Taiwan (body, facts.birthDate, facts.birthPlace, FAQ)
claims.note: Britannica gives 17 Feb 1963, Tainan. CHM gives 1963, Tainan.

claims.claim: He is 63 years old (as of 2026-10-26; summary, metaDescription, FAQ, opening line)
claims.note: 1963-02-17 to 2026-10-26 is 63 years. The Britannica page shows 'age 61' only because it is a stale snapshot.

claims.claim: At about age nine he arrived in the US from Thailand with his brother and was sent to the Oneida Baptist Institute, a religious boarding school in Kentucky for 'problem' boys
claims.note: Britannica: the brothers were sent to their uncle in Tacoma, who sent them to Oneida, a religious reform school for 'difficult' children.

claims.claim: At 30, in 1993, he was founding NVIDIA
claims.note: Founded April 1993, when he was 30.

claims.claim: His birth name was Jen-Hsun Huang
claims.note: Britannica lists 'Also known as Jen-Hsun Huang'. CHM does not mention it.

claims.claim: At five the family moved to Thailand; at about nine he and his brother were sent to an uncle in Tacoma, who enrolled them in the Kentucky school
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: About two years later the parents arrived, pulled the sons out, and the family settled near Portland, Oregon
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: He finished high school in Aloha in 1981
claims.note: Britannica: Aloha High School, graduated 1981.

claims.claim: BSEE in electrical engineering from Oregon State in 1984; met Lori Mills there and married her
claims.note: Britannica gives the 1984 degree and says he met Lori Mills at OSU and the pair later married. The marriage is reported on the record.

claims.claim: About one year at AMD, then LSI Logic from 1985 to 1993, where he ran a division
claims.note: NVIDIA bio: LSI Logic 1985–1993, AMD 1984–1985. Britannica: he rose to director of a division.

claims.claim: He earned a master's in electrical engineering at Stanford while working
claims.note: Britannica: 'While working, he returned to school' and got the MSEE at Stanford.

claims.claim: NVIDIA was founded in April 1993 by Huang, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, and Huang was chosen to be CEO
claims.note: Britannica gives April 1993 and says the other two selected him as CEO. CHM confirms 1993 and the three founders.

claims.claim: The trio started with US$40,000; VC firms then put in US$20 million
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: Huang has been president, CEO and board member since the start
claims.note: NVIDIA bio, retrieved 2026-10-26, says 'since its inception'. Still current.

claims.claim: NVIDIA went public in 1999
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: In 1999 it launched the GeForce 256, billed as the world's first GPU, combining transform, lighting and rendering
claims.note: The quoted Portuguese is a paraphrase of CHM's 'world's first graphics processing unit'.

claims.claim: CUDA (2006) allowed NVIDIA GPUs to be used for general-purpose computing
claims.note: Matches CHM.

claims.claim: Six years later (2012) AlexNet was trained on NVIDIA GPUs and the company pivoted to accelerated computing for AI
claims.note: 2012 minus 2006 is six years. CHM supports the pivot.

claims.claim: In 2018 Huang said GPU performance was growing faster than Moore's law predicts; the press called it 'Huang's law'
claims.note: Britannica: 2018 GTC, 25x in five years, dubbed 'Huang's law'.

claims.claim: Fox Business reported NVIDIA as the first company to reach US$5 trillion in market value
claims.note: Fox Business article dated 2025-10-30. The article gives no date for the milestone and ties it causally to the AI shift ('O resultado apareceu...'), which is the writer's framing.

claims.claim: Fortune named him Businessperson of the Year in 2017; HBR ranked him the world's best-performing CEO in 2019
claims.note: Both facts are on the NVIDIA bio and in Britannica. The HBR list is the 100 best-performing CEOs over their tenure.

claims.claim: Time included him in its 100 most influential people in 2021
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: In 2024 the Computer History Museum named him a Fellow
claims.note: CHM: '2024 Fellow'.

claims.claim: Time's 2025 Person of the Year went to the 'Architects of AI', which include Huang
claims.note: Fast Company/AP, 2025-12-11, lists Huang among the eight.

claims.claim: The IEEE awarded him the 2026 Medal of Honor
claims.note: Both sources confirm. The ieee-honors source says it was presented in April 2026.

claims.claim: With his wife he created the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation in 2007
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: Summary: NVIDIA focused on AI computing from 2012
claims.note: Backed by the CHM 2012 AlexNet pivot in the body.

claims.claim: metaDescription: onde trabalhou antes (AMD e LSI Logic)
claims.note: Body states the jobs; confirmed.

claims.claim: Em 29 de outubro de 2025 a NVIDIA fechou valendo US$ 5,03 trilhões, primeira empresa a atingir esse valor
claims.note: Confirmed in the es/de reviews.

claims.claim: Added details: uncle mistook Oneida for a prestigious school; daily toilet cleaning; father via Carrier programme; ten English words a day; Denny's; Dreamcast crisis and Irimajiri investment; tattoo at $100; GTC 2018 25x; supercomputers; Apple/Microsoft past $4tn; US$500bn orders; Fox interview quote; CHM Fellow citation
claims.note: Each was confirmed against the same source in the jensen-huang/en or /es review.

valueNote: Clear timeline with concrete, sourced details (Oneida, Denny's, the Sega crisis, the 25x GTC figure, the dated US$5 trillion close) and a translated primary quote; more than the usual short profiles.
summary: Re-check after fixes. 1 flagged claim(s) from the previous review were corrected or removed: metaDescription no longer promises reasons for AMD/LSI Logic; the US$5 trillion line is dated 29 October 2025 with no causal claim; 'nasceu Jen-Hsun' is now 'também conhecido como'; the page was expanded with facts confirmed in the en/es reviews against the same sources (Oneida mix-up and toilet cleaning, parents, ten English words a day, Denny's, Sega Dreamcast crisis, tattoo, GTC 2018 25x figure, supercomputers, US$500bn orders, CHM Fellow citation, Fox interview quote).
